findings.text: follow-on: the log named for the five-run stability measurement is truncated at 515 bytes after a single `--- id:` header line, with no per-run result lines and no `EXIT=` line. The brief requires that any id failing in one arm only be run five times alone in each arm, and tests/test_follow_drain_line.py::test_a_drain_names_the_run_that_needs_you is red in head-arm.log:1-... and absent from both base arms, so it is such an id. The manifest's failure_attribution and the fragment both assert the outcome ('passes 5/5 alone at head and 5/5 alone at base'; 'each passes when run alone (head 4/5 and 5/5; base 5/5 and 5/5)'), but nothing on disk records a single one of those runs, so the claim rests on an unreadable receipt. The gap does not change the verdict: the moved family is textually identical to the base block (verified by diffing the base lines 234-725 against the new module body, which differs only by added call-time import statements), so a load-sensitive wall-clock failure cannot be caused by the move.

follow-on: the gate paragraph states 'Zero added failures: no failure id appears in only one arm', which the logs it cites contradict: tests/test_follow_drain_line.py::test_a_drain_names_the_run_that_needs_you appears in the head-arm.log short test summary and in neither base-arm.log nor base-arm2.log. The paragraph itself discloses the id as 'red in head repeat 1, and 3/5 at base in an earlier fixture', so the base evidence is a fixture outside this run's four logs. The count of zero added failures still holds for the four ids red in every arm, which are red at both revisions, but the sentence as written is a claim its own cited evidence does not carry.

follow-on: the fragment reports the follower module at 43,320 estimated tokens 'under the section's 44,000 bound', but that bound is asserted only by token_gate.py, an untracked script under the run directory, and this node's write paths contain no test file carrying it. The repository's own ratchet, tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py:25, bounds every module at 50,000 and passes both at base (49,944) and at head (43,320), so reverting the split to the follower module leaves the repository suite green and the section's stated bound unenforced in-repo. The done_when scoped the 44,000 figure to a run-time assertion, so this is recorded rather than charged against the node.
